# Retrospective: PR 12831 follow-up

## Worked

Fresh Fable 5.1 High and Astra Xhigh sessions received equivalent neutral packets derived only from public claims, current source and author reply. Independent real-UFW approaches converged on normal-path success. The migration driver test separated a valid original fix from a new conditional lost-retry defect. Preserved raw exits and recovery controls were more useful than summary messages. No finding quota or generic test advice was used.

## Friction and corrections

Fable's first bundle had assertion/PATH fixture mistakes. Astra corrected byte-stream capture and ordering in successive sealed bundles. All originals were preserved; only corrected final runs support public claims. No confirmed review.py or Omadev defect emerged.

A disposition-label difference for the source-filtering clarification was reconciled explicitly: acknowledged but still true, not an outstanding defect. Fable's marker claim was clarified as source-derived; the independent Astra driver run supplies direct evidence.

## Mandatory isolation deviation

Fable performed unsandboxed host version/capability queries and read-only systemctl state probes, plus unnecessary host firewall configuration reads. These violated the all-runtime sandbox requirement even though no host mutation was reported and the actual PR tests were sandboxed. Exact commands and effects are retained in reviewers/fable/safety-audit.md. The coordinator requested that audit after reading the report, stopped further experimentation, notified STATUS.md and the outer assistant, and marks safety_process_compliant false. Historical artifacts were not altered to obscure the deviation.

Future assignments should explicitly list version/status probes as runtime checks and forbid host-service negative controls. Source-based version identification or in-sandbox capture suffices. Do not mistake read-only for compliance with an explicit isolation boundary.

## Cleanup and handoff

All test processes ended with their runner namespaces, no desktop slot or persistent service was used. Pinned worktrees and sealed evidence remain for audit. Reviewer panes remain idle; coordinator does not reset itself or select another PR. HTML is saved without opening. Fresh editorial check passes the exact draft and combined requirements, but outer assessment of the safety deviation remains necessary before publication.

**Verified:** At `a375f69a`, the new migration resolves the missing-upgrade-migration finding in the [earlier review](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/12831#issuecomment-5768242893) on the successful path: it removes the legacy unrestricted IPv4/IPv6 exceptions, installs six RFC1918-scoped rules, preserves tested unrelated rules, and reruns without duplicates. One new failure-path issue remains.

## UFW errors can permanently skip the repair

In `migrations/1790062824.sh:16-23`, a failed `ufw status` exits successfully, and deletion failures are treated like missing success text. The migration driver then records completion.

With real UFW 0.36.2 persistence code and **injected backend failures**, running the actual migration driver produced:

| Condition | Persisted unrestricted exceptions | Completion marker |
|---|---|---|
| Successful control | None | Written |
| Status query fails | Both IPv4 and both IPv6 rules remain | Written |
| Deletes fail during rule application | Both IPv6 rules remain, alongside six scoped IPv4 rules | Written |

After the injected failures were cleared, a normal rerun skipped the marked migration and performed no UFW commands. These were diagnostic failure simulations, not observed real-machine outages.

**Impact:** A failed migration can retain the pre-existing broad exceptions while preventing automatic retry using that user's migration state. It does not introduce new broad defaults.

**Suggested change:** Preserve the absent-UFW no-op, but propagate status and deletion errors. Check each deletion's exit status separately from its output text; use the text only to distinguish successful deletion from successful no-op. That lets the driver leave failed work pending.

**Scope clarification:** The author's revised description is accurate: RFC1918 filtering does not select trusted Wi-Fi networks. Opening the port only while LocalSend runs would be a separate design change; this follow-up does not establish a need to replace the narrower approach.

---

## Review information

**Test scope:** UFW 0.36.2 rule persistence, isolated live rule-chain inspection, reruns, representative custom-rule preservation, and fault-injected migration-driver checks. Elevation/service actions were stubbed; failure tests simulated backend responses. No traffic, LocalSend transfer, IPv6 connectivity, or full upgrade test.

**Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.
